title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 117 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 581–584 (Night 117, continuing directly from nights-116), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 117 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. ʿAzīz goes on with his tale to Tāj al-Mulūk. His cousin ʿAzīza, who cannot leave the house, sends him back to the garden with one warning: eat nothing, for eating brings sleep. He finds the pavilion laid out again, cannot resist the chicken, the sweets and the saffron pudding, and sleeps till sunrise; he wakes in the emptied pavilion with a knucklebone, a stick from the game of ṭāb, a date-stone and a carob seed on his belly. At home he curses ʿAzīza, who has been weeping over verses of her love for him, and then begs her to read the signs: his body was there but not his heart; a true lover would never have tasted sleep; a lover's heart is weary, and he must bear the parting with the patience of Job. She feeds him, dresses him in a splendid suit, and sends him back a third night, where he sits holding his eyes open with his fingers as darkness falls. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventeenth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and seventeenth night,
sentences.n: al-sābiʿata ʿashara, “seventeenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر beside the feminine night, and it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ قَالَ لِتَاجِ الْمُلُوكِ فَقُلْتُ لِابْنَةِ عَمِّي دُلِّينِي عَلَى شَيْءٍ أَفْعَلُهُ وَارْحَمِينِى يَرْحَمُكِ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba qāla li-tāji al-mulūki fa-qultu li-ibnati ʿammī dullīnī ʿalā shayʾin afʿaluhu wa-irḥamīnī yarḥamuki allāhu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the youth said to Tāj al-Mulūk: And I said to the daughter of my uncle: Guide me to a thing I may do, and have mercy on me — God have mercy on you!
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man said to Tāj al-Mulūk: I said to my cousin, “Tell me something I can do, and have pity on me, and may God have pity on you!”
sentences.n: The night opens by going back over the last lines of the night before. yarḥamuki allāhu, “God have mercy on you”: a wish, the usual formula of entreaty. وارحمينى is printed with ى for final ي.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ تُحِبُّنِى مَحَبَّةً عَظِيمَةً
sentences.tr: wa-kānat tuḥibbunī maḥabbatan ʿaẓīmatan
sentences.l: And she loved me with a great love.
sentences.i: For she loved me dearly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَلَى رَأْسِي وَعَيْنِي وَلٰكِنْ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي قَدْ قُلْتُ لَكَ مِرَارًا لَوْ كُنْتُ أَدْخُلُ وَأَخْرُجُ لَكُنْتُ أَجْمَعُ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهَا فِي أَقْرَبِ زَمَنٍ وَأُغَطِّيكُمَا بِذَيْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿalā raʾsī wa-ʿaynī wa-lākin yā bna ʿammī qad qultu laka mirāran law kuntu adkhulu wa-akhruju la-kuntu ajmaʿu baynaka wa-baynahā fī aqrabi zamanin wa-ughaṭṭīkumā bi-dhaylī
sentences.l: And she said: On my head and my eye! But, O son of my uncle, I have said to you many-times: if I were (one who) goes-in and goes-out, I would bring-together between you and her in the nearest time, and cover you-two with my skirt.
sentences.i: She said, “With all my heart. But, cousin, I have told you again and again: if I were free to come and go, I would bring you and her together in no time, and cover the two of you with the hem of my robe.
sentences.n: ʿalā raʾsī wa-ʿaynī, “on my head and my eye”: gladly, at once — the formula of willing assent. kuntu adkhulu wa-akhruju, “I were one who goes in and goes out”: kāna with an imperfect describes a habit or a standing condition, here the freedom to leave the house. To cover lovers with one’s skirt (dhayl) is to shield them and keep their secret.

sentences.t: وَلَا أَفْعَلُ مَعَكَ هَذَا إِلَّا لِقَصْدِ رِضَاكَ وَإِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَبْذُلُ غَايَةَ الْجُهْدِ فِى الْجَمْعِ بَيْنَكُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-lā afʿalu maʿaka hādhā illā li-qaṣdi riḍāka wa-in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā abdhulu ghāyata al-juhdi fī al-jamʿi baynakumā
sentences.l: And I do not do this with you except for the aim of your contentment; and if God, exalted is He, wills, I will spend the utmost of effort in the bringing-together between you-two.
sentences.i: Whatever I do for you, I do only to please you; and if God most high wills it, I will do everything in my power to bring you together.

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنِ اسْمَعْ قَوْلِي وَأَطِعْ أَمْرِى وَاذْهَبْ إِلَى نَفْسِ ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ وَاقْعُدْ هُنَاكَ فَإِذَا كَانَ وَقْتُ الْعِشَاءِ فَاجْلِسْ فِى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي كُنْتَ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākini ismaʿ qawlī wa-aṭiʿ amrī wa-idhhab ilā nafsi dhālika al-makāni wa-uqʿud hunāka fa-idhā kāna waqtu al-ʿishāʾi fa-ijlis fī al-mawḍiʿi alladhī kunta fīhi
sentences.l: But hear my saying and obey my command, and go to the self (of) that place and sit there; and when it is the time of the night-prayer, sit in the spot which you were in.
sentences.i: But listen to what I say and do as I tell you. Go back to that very place and stay there, and when the hour of the evening prayer comes, sit where you sat before.
sentences.n: nafsi dhālika al-makāni, “the self of that place”: nafs before a noun means “the very same”. waqt al-ʿishāʾ: the hour of the last prayer of the day, after nightfall.

sentences.t: وَاحْذَرْ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ شَيًاْ لِأَنَّ الْأَكْلَ يَجْلِبُ النَّوْمَ وَإِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَنَامَ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَأْتِي لَكَ حَتَّى يَمْضِى مِنَ اللَّيْلِ رُبْعُهُ كَفَاكَ اللَّهُ شَرَّمَا
sentences.tr: wa-iḥdhar an taʾkula shayʾan li-anna al-akla yajlibu al-nawma wa-iyyāka an tanāma fa-innahā lā taʾtī laka ḥattā yamḍī mina al-layli rubʿuhu kafāka allāhu sharra-mā
sentences.l: And beware that you eat a thing, because eating brings sleep; and you — beware that you sleep! For she does not come to you until there has passed of the night its quarter. God suffice you (against) the evil of what (may be)!
sentences.i: Take care not to eat anything, for eating brings on sleep; and on no account fall asleep, for she will not come to you until a quarter of the night has gone. God keep you from harm!”
sentences.n: iyyāka an tanāma, “you — that you sleep!”: iyyā- with a pronoun is the form of warning, “beware of…”. lā taʾtī laka, “she does not come to you”: Middle Arabic gives atā a li- where Classical takes a direct object. kafāka allāhu sharra-mā: the print has شرّما as one word, “the evil of what…”, which reads as a phrase cut short; it may be a misprint for شرّها, “its evil”, but that is a guess, so the print is kept and translated by the general sense. شيا is the print’s spelling of shayʾan, with a sukūn printed over the alif, kept here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا فَرِحْتُ وَصِرْتُ أَدْعُو اللَّهَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā fariḥtu wa-ṣirtu adʿū allāha an yaʾtiya al-laylu
sentences.l: And when I heard her speech, I rejoiced, and I began calling-on God that the night come.
sentences.i: When I heard what she said I was glad, and I began praying to God for the night to come.
sentences.n: ṣirtu adʿū: ṣāra with an imperfect, “I began to …”, as often in this text.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَتَى اللَّيْلُ أَرَدْتُ الِانْصِرَافَ فَقَالَتْ لِي ابْنَةُ عَمِّى إِذَا اجْتَمَعْتَ بِهَا فَاذْكُرْ لَهَا الْبَيْتَ الْمُتَقَدِّمَ وَقْتَ انْصِرَافِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā atā al-laylu aradtu al-inṣirāfa fa-qālat lī ibnatu ʿammī idhā ijtamaʿta bihā fa-udhkur lahā al-bayta al-mutaqaddima waqta inṣirāfika
sentences.l: And when the night came, I wanted the going-away; and the daughter of my uncle said to me: When you meet with her, mention to her the verse gone-before, at the time of your going-away.
sentences.i: When night came and I was about to go, my cousin said to me, “When you are with her, recite to her the line of verse I told you before, at the moment you take your leave.”
sentences.n: al-bayt al-mutaqaddim, “the verse that went before”: the line of poetry ʿAzīza gave him earlier to recite to the woman. ijtamaʿa bi-, “meet with, be together with”: bi- marks the person met.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا عَلَى الرَّأْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā ʿalā al-raʾsi wa-al-ʿayni
sentences.l: And I said to her: On the head and the eye!
sentences.i: “With all my heart,” I told her.
sentences.n: الراس: the print’s spelling of al-raʾs, without the hamza.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَرَجْتُ وَذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَجَدْتُ الْمَكَانَ مُهَيَّأً عَلَى الْحَالَةِ الَّتِي رَأَيْتُهَا أَوَّلًا وَفِيهِ مَايُحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ وَالشَّرَابِ وَالنُّقْلِ وَالْمَشْمُومِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharajtu wa-dhahabtu ilā al-bustāni wajadtu al-makāna muhayyaʾan ʿalā al-ḥālati allatī raʾaytuhā awwalan wa-fīhi mā yuḥtāju ilayhi mina al-ṭaʿāmi wa-al-sharābi wa-al-nuqli wa-al-mashmūmi wa-ghayri dhālika
sentences.l: And when I went out and went to the garden, I found the place made-ready in the state in which I saw it first, and in it what is needed of food and drink and dessert-fruits and smelled-things and other than that.
sentences.i: So I went out and made my way to the garden, and found the place laid out just as I had seen it the first time, with everything one could want: food and drink, dried fruits and nuts, sweet-smelling flowers and the rest.
sentences.n: The print has البهتان (al-buhtān, “slander”), a misprint for البستان (al-bustān, “the garden”), corrected here. al-nuql: dried fruits and nuts, taken with wine. al-mashmūm, “what is smelled”: flowers and other scented things. mā yuḥtāju ilayhi, “what is needed”, is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعْتُ الْمَقْعَدَ وَشَمَمْتُ رَائِحَةَ الطَّعَامِ فَاشْتَاقَتْ نَفْسِي إِلَيْهِ فَمَنَعْتُهَا مِرَارًا فَلَمْ أَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَنْعِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿtu al-maqʿada wa-shamamtu rāʾiḥata al-ṭaʿāmi fa-ishtāqat nafsī ilayhi fa-manaʿtuhā mirāran fa-lam aqdir ʿalā manʿihā
sentences.l: And I went-up (into) the sitting-place, and smelled the smell of the food, and my soul longed for it; and I held-it-back many-times, and I was not able to hold-it-back.
sentences.i: I climbed up into the alcove and smelled the food, and my appetite craved it. Again and again I held myself back, but I could not hold out.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa with a direct object, “go up into”. nafs, “self, appetite”, is feminine, hence ishtāqat and manaʿtuhā.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَى السُّفْرَةِ وَكَشَفْتُ غِطَاءَهَا فَوَجَدْتُ صَحْنَ دَجَاجٍ وَحَوْلَهُ أَرْبَعُ زَبَادِى مِنَ الطَّعَامِ فِيهَا أَرْبَعَةُ أَلْوَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-ataytu ilā al-sufrati wa-kashaftu ghiṭāʾahā fa-wajadtu ṣaḥna dajājin wa-ḥawlahu arbaʿu zabādī mina al-ṭaʿāmi fīhā arbaʿatu alwānin
sentences.l: And I rose and came to the food-cloth and uncovered its covering, and I found a dish of chicken, and around it four bowls of food, in them four colours.
sentences.i: So I got up, went to the table-cloth and lifted the cover, and found a dish of chicken, and round it four bowls holding four different dishes.
sentences.n: sufra: the cloth or low tray on which a meal is laid. alwān, “colours”, is the usual word for the separate dishes of a meal. zabādī, “bowls” (singular zubdiyya), is printed with ى for final ي.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ مِنْ كُلِّ لَوْنٍ لُقْمَةً وَأَكَلْتُ مَاتَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْحَلْوَى وَأَكَلْتُ قِطْعَةَ لَحْمٍ وَشَرِبْتُ مِنَ الزَّرْدَةِ وَأَعْجَبَتْنِي فَأَكْثَرْتُ الشُّرْبَ مِنْهَا بِالْمِلْعَقَةِ حَتَّى شَبِعْتُ وَامْتَلَأَتْ بَطْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu min kulli lawnin luqmatan wa-akaltu mā tayassara mina al-ḥalwā wa-akaltu qiṭʿata laḥmin wa-sharibtu mina al-zardati wa-aʿjabatnī fa-akthartu al-shurba minhā bi-al-milʿaqati ḥattā shabiʿtu wa-imtalaʾat baṭnī
sentences.l: And I ate of every colour a mouthful, and I ate what was-easy of the sweetmeat, and I ate a piece of meat, and I drank of the zarda, and it pleased me, and I made-much the drinking of it with the spoon, until I was sated and my belly was filled.
sentences.i: I ate a mouthful of each dish, and as much of the sweets as came to hand, and a piece of meat; and I took some of the saffron pudding, and liked it so well that I kept spooning it down until I was full and my belly was stuffed.
sentences.n: al-zarda: rice sweetened and coloured with saffron, eaten with a spoon — hence “drank of it with the spoon”. mā tayassara, “what was easy”, that is, whatever came to hand, is printed as one word. baṭn, “belly”, is treated as feminine here, as in the night before.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ انْطَبَقَتْ أَجْفَانِي فَأَخَذْتُ وِسَادَةً وَوَضَعْتُهَا تَحْتَ رَأْسِي وَقُلْتُ لَعَلِّي أَتَّكِئُ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا أَنَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika inṭabaqat ajfānī fa-akhadhtu wisādatan wa-waḍaʿtuhā taḥta raʾsī wa-qultu laʿallī attakiʾu ʿalayhā wa-lā anāmu
sentences.l: And after that my eyelids closed-together; and I took a cushion and put it under my head, and said: Perhaps I (may) lean on it and not sleep.
sentences.i: After that my eyelids kept falling shut. I took a cushion and put it under my head, telling myself, “Perhaps I can lean on it without falling asleep.”

sentences.t: فَأَغْمَضْتُ عَيْنِي وَنِمْتُ وَمَا انْتَبَهْتُ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ
sentences.tr: fa-aghmaḍtu ʿaynī wa-nimtu wa-mā intabahtu ḥattā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu
sentences.l: And I closed my eye and slept, and I did not wake until the sun rose.
sentences.i: Then I shut my eyes and slept, and did not wake until the sun was up.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ عَلَى بَطْنِي كَعْبَ عَظْمٍ وَفَرْدَةَ طَابٍ وَنَوَايَةَ بَلَحٍ وَبِزْرَةَ خَرُّوبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu ʿalā baṭnī kaʿba ʿaẓmin wa-fardata ṭābin wa-nawāyata balaḥin wa-bizrata kharrūbin
sentences.l: And I found on my belly a heel of bone, and a single-piece of ṭāb, and a stone of dates, and a seed of carob.
sentences.i: And I found on my belly a knucklebone, a stick from the game of ṭāb, a date-stone and a carob seed.
sentences.n: kaʿb ʿaẓm, “a heel of bone”: a knucklebone, the small ankle bone thrown like a die in games. ṭāb: a game played by throwing flat sticks; farda, “a single one”, is one of the sticks. nawāya is the everyday word for nawāh, “fruit-stone”; balaḥ, fresh dates — the print points the word بَلَح. bizra, “seed”; kharrūb, “carob”.

sentences.t: وَلَيْسَ فِى الْمَكَانِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ فَرْشٍ وَلَا غَيْرِهِ وَكَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ بِالْأَمْسِ
sentences.tr: wa-laysa fī al-makāni shayʾun min farshin wa-lā ghayrihi wa-kaʾannahu lam yakun fīhi shayʾun bi-al-amsi
sentences.l: And there was not in the place a thing, of furnishing or other than it; and (it was) as if there had not been in it a thing yesterday.
sentences.i: There was nothing left in the place, no carpets or anything else; it was as if nothing had been there the day before.
sentences.n: bi-al-amsi, “yesterday”: bi- here marks a point in time.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَنَفَضْتُ الْجَمِيعَ عَنِّي وَخَرَجْتُ وَأَنَا مُغْتَاظٌ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلْتُ إِلَي الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-nafaḍtu al-jamīʿa ʿannī wa-kharajtu wa-anā mughtāẓun ilā an waṣaltu ilā al-bayti
sentences.l: And I rose and shook the whole (of it) off me, and went out, I being enraged, until I arrived at the house.
sentences.i: I got up, shook it all off me and left, seething with anger, and so came home.
sentences.n: The second ilā is printed الي, with final ي for ى.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي تُصَعِّدُ الزَّفَرَاتِ وَتُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu ibnata ʿammī tuṣaʿʿidu al-zafarāti wa-tunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And I found the daughter of my uncle sending-up the sighs and reciting these verses:
sentences.i: There I found my cousin heaving deep sighs and reciting these lines:

sentences.t:
جَسَدٌ نَاحِلٌ وَقَلْبٌ جَرِيحٌ * وَدُمُوعٌ عَلَى الْخُدُودِ تَسِيحُ
وَحَبِيبٌ صَعْبُ التَّجَنِّي وَلٰكِنْ * كُلَّمَا يَفْعَلُ الْمَلِيحُ مَلِيحُ
يَابْنَ عَمِّي مَلَأْتَ بِالْوَجْدِ قَلْبِي * اِنَّ طَرْفِي مِنْ الدُّمُوعِ قَرِيحُ
sentences.tr:
jasadun nāḥilun wa-qalbun jarīḥun * wa-dumūʿun ʿalā al-khudūdi tasīḥu
wa-ḥabībun ṣaʿbu al-tajannī wa-lākin * kullamā yafʿalu al-malīḥu malīḥu
yā bna ʿammī malaʾta bi-al-wajdi qalbī * inna ṭarfī mina al-dumūʿi qarīḥu
sentences.n: al-tajannī: charging someone with a fault they have not committed, the caprice of the beloved. kullamā, printed as one word, stands here for kullu mā, “all that”: all that the fair one does is fair. min al-dumūʿi: the print points مِنْ with a sukūn before the article; in reading, the nūn takes its usual connecting vowel, mina al-dumūʿi. ṭarf, “eye, glance”.

sentences.t: فَنَهَرْتُ ابْنَةَ عَمِّي وَشَتَمْتُهَا فَبَكَتْ ثُمَّ مَسَحَتْ دُمُوعَهَا وَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيَّ وَقَبَّلَتْنِي وَأَخَذَتْ تَضُمُّنِي إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَأَنَا أَتَبَاعَدُ عَنْهَا وَأُعَاتِبُ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-nahartu ibnata ʿammī wa-shatamtuhā fa-bakat thumma masaḥat dumūʿahā wa-aqbalat ʿalayya wa-qabbalatnī wa-akhadhat taḍummunī ilā ṣadrihā wa-anā atabāʿadu ʿanhā wa-uʿātibu nafsī
sentences.l: And I rebuked the daughter of my uncle and reviled her, and she wept; then she wiped her tears and came-forward to me and kissed me, and began pressing me to her breast, I drawing-away from her and reproaching myself.
sentences.i: I shouted at my cousin and cursed her, and she wept; then she wiped away her tears, came to me and kissed me, and held me to her breast, while I pulled away from her, blaming myself.
sentences.n: akhadhat taḍummunī: akhadha with an imperfect, “began to …”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي يَا بْنَ عَمِّي كَأَنَّكَ نِمْتَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī yā bna ʿammī kaʾannaka nimta fī hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: And she said to me: O son of my uncle, (it is) as if you slept in this night.
sentences.i: She said to me, “Cousin, it looks as though you slept last night.”

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا نَعَمْ وَلٰكِنَّنِي لَمَّا انْتَبَهْتُ وَجَدْتُ كَعْبَ عَظْمٍ وَفَرْدَةَ طَابٍ وَنَوَايَةَ بَلَحٍ وَبِزْرَةَ خَرُّوبٍ وَمَا أَدْرِي لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلَتْ هٰكَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā naʿam wa-lākinnanī lammā intabahtu wajadtu kaʿba ʿaẓmin wa-fardata ṭābin wa-nawāyata balaḥin wa-bizrata kharrūbin wa-mā adrī li-ayyi shayʾin faʿalat hākadhā
sentences.l: And I said to her: Yes; but I, when I woke, found a heel of bone, and a single-piece of ṭāb, and a stone of dates, and a seed of carob; and I do not know for what thing she did thus.
sentences.i: “Yes,” I told her, “and when I woke I found a knucklebone, a ṭāb stick, a date-stone and a carob seed; and I do not know why she did it.”
sentences.n: li-ayyi shayʾin, “for what thing”: li-, “for”, asking the reason.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَيْتُ وَأَقْبَلْتُ عَلَيْهَا وَقُلْتُ لَهَا فَسِّرِي لِي إِشَارَةَ فِعْلِهَا هَذَا وَقُولِي لِي مَاذَا أَفْعَلُ وَسَاعِدِينِي عَلَى الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma bakaytu wa-aqbaltu ʿalayhā wa-qultu lahā fassirī lī ishārata fiʿlihā hādhā wa-qūlī lī mādhā afʿalu wa-sāʿidīnī ʿalā alladhī anā fīhi
sentences.l: Then I wept, and came-forward to her and said to her: Explain to me the sign of this doing of hers, and tell me what I shall do, and help me in that which I am in.
sentences.i: Then I wept, and turned to her and said, “Explain to me what she meant by this, and tell me what I should do, and help me in this plight of mine.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَلَى الرَّأْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ أَمَّا فَرْدَةُ الطَّابِ الَّتِي وَضَعَتْهَا عَلَى بَطْنِكَ فَإِنَّهَا تُشِيرُ لَكَ بِهَا إِلَى أَنَّكَ حَضَرْتَ وَقَلْبُكَ غَائِبٌ وَكَأَنَّهَا تَقُولُ لَكَ لَيْسَ الْعِشْقُ هٰكَذَا فَلَا تَعُدَّ نَفْسَكَ مِنَ الْعَاشِقِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿalā al-raʾsi wa-al-ʿayni ammā fardatu al-ṭābi allatī waḍaʿathā ʿalā baṭnika fa-innahā tushīru laka bihā ilā annaka ḥaḍarta wa-qalbuka ghāʾibun wa-kaʾannahā taqūlu laka laysa al-ʿishqu hākadhā fa-lā taʿudda nafsaka mina al-ʿāshiqīna
sentences.l: And she said: On the head and the eye! As for the single-piece of ṭāb which she put on your belly, she points out to you with it that you were present and your heart absent; and (it is) as if she says to you: Love is not thus, so do not count yourself among the lovers.
sentences.i: “Gladly,” she said. “The ṭāb stick she laid on your belly is her sign to you that you came, but your heart was not there. It is as if she were saying: This is not what love is; do not count yourself among lovers.
sentences.n: tushīru laka bihā ilā, “she points out to you with it (to the fact) that”: ashāra ilā, “point to, indicate”, with bi- for the thing one points with. ʿAzīza reads three of the four signs here; the knucklebone she leaves unexplained.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا نَوَايَةُ الْبَلَحِ فَإِنَّهَا تُشِيرُ لَكَ بِهَا إِلَى أَنَّكَ لَوْ كُنْتَ عَاشِقًا لَكَانَ قَلْبُكَ مُحْتَرِقًا بِالْغَرَامِ وَلَمْ تَذُقْ لَذِيذَ الْمَنَامِ فَإِنَّ لَذَّةَ الْحُبِّ كَتَمْرَةٍ أَلْهَبَتْ فِى الْفُؤَادِ جَمْرَةً
sentences.tr: wa-ammā nawāyatu al-balaḥi fa-innahā tushīru laka bihā ilā annaka law kunta ʿāshiqan la-kāna qalbuka muḥtariqan bi-al-gharāmi wa-lam tadhuq ladhīdha al-manāmi fa-inna ladhdhata al-ḥubbi ka-tamratin alhabat fī al-fuʾādi jamratan
sentences.l: And as for the stone of dates, she points out to you with it that if you were a lover, your heart would be burning with passion, and you would not have tasted the sweet of sleep; for the sweetness of love is like a date (that) has kindled in the heart an ember.
sentences.i: The date-stone is her sign that if you were really in love your heart would be burning with passion, and you would never have tasted the sweetness of sleep; for the sweetness of love is like a date that sets a live coal glowing in the heart.
sentences.n: The rhymes fall in pairs, gharām / manām and tamra / jamra: the date-stone is read through a jingle on the date. bi-al-gharāmi, “with passion”: bi- of cause; ka-, “like”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بِزْرَةُ الْخَرُّوبِ فَإِنَّهَا تُشِيرُ لَكَ بِهَا إِلَى أَنَّ قَلْبَ الْمُحِبِّ مَتْعُوبٌ وَتَقُولُ لَكَ اصْبِرْ عَلَى فِرَاقِنَا صَبْرَ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā bizratu al-kharrūbi fa-innahā tushīru laka bihā ilā anna qalba al-muḥibbi matʿūbun wa-taqūlu laka iṣbir ʿalā firāqinā ṣabra ayyūba
sentences.l: And as for the seed of carob, she points out to you with it that the heart of the lover is wearied, and she says to you: Be patient over our parting (with) the patience of Job.
sentences.i: And the carob seed is her sign that a lover’s heart is a weary one, and she is telling you: Bear our parting with the patience of Job.”
sentences.n: matʿūb, “wearied”: an everyday passive participle where Classical says mutʿab. The carob too is read through its rhyme, kharrūb / matʿūb / Ayyūb. Job (Ayyūb) is proverbial for patience.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ هَذَا التَّفْسِيرَ انْطَلَقَتْ فِي فُؤَادِى النِّيرَانُ وَزَادَتْ بِقَلْبِي الْأَحْزَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu hādhā al-tafsīra inṭalaqat fī fuʾādī al-nīrānu wa-zādat bi-qalbī al-aḥzānu
sentences.l: And when I heard this explanation, the fires were let-loose in my inmost-heart (fuʾād), and the griefs increased in my heart.
sentences.i: When I heard her explanation, fire broke out in my heart and my sorrows grew.
sentences.n: nīrān / aḥzān: rhymed prose. bi-qalbī, “in my heart”: bi- of place.

sentences.t: فَصِحْتُ وَقُلْتُ قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ النَّوْمَ لِقِلَّةِ بَخْتِي
sentences.tr: fa-ṣiḥtu wa-qultu qaddara allāhu ʿalayya al-nawma li-qillati bakhtī
sentences.l: And I cried-out and said: God decreed upon me the sleep, for the scantness of my luck.
sentences.i: I cried out, “God decreed that I should sleep — that is how poor my luck is!”
sentences.n: bakht, “luck, fortune”, is a loanword from Persian. li-qillati, “because of the scantness”: li- of cause.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُلْتُ لَهَا يَا ابْنَةَ عَمِّي بِحَيَاتِي عِنْدَكِ أَنْ تُدَبِّرِى لِي حِيلَةً أَتَوَصَّلُ بِهَا إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qultu lahā yā ibnata ʿammī bi-ḥayātī ʿindaki an tudabbirī lī ḥīlatan atawaṣṣalu bihā ilayhā
sentences.l: Then I said to her: O daughter of my uncle, by my life with you, (I beg) that you contrive for me a stratagem (that) I may reach by it to her.
sentences.i: Then I said to her, “Cousin, by my life, which is dear to you, think out some way for me to reach her.”
sentences.n: bi-ḥayātī ʿindaki, “by my life (as it is) with you”: an oath by something the hearer holds dear, bi- of oaths; the an-clause after it is the request itself.

sentences.t: فَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ يَا عَزِيزُ يَا بْنَ عَمِّي إِنَّ قَلْبِي مَلْأٰنُ بِالْفِكْرِ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-bakat wa-qālat yā ʿazīzu yā bna ʿammī inna qalbī malʾānu bi-al-fikri wa-lā aqdiru an atakallama
sentences.l: And she wept and said: O ʿAzīz, O son of my uncle, my heart is full with thought, and I am not able to speak.
sentences.i: She wept and said, “ʿAzīz, cousin, my heart is so full of care that I cannot speak.
sentences.n: malʾān, “full”, is printed ملأن, without its long alif. fikr, “thought”, here anxious thought, care.

sentences.t: وَلٰكِنْ رُحِ اللَّيْلَةَ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ وَاحْذَرْ أَنْ تَنَامَ فَإِنَّكَ تَبْلُغُ الْمَرَامَ هَذَا هُوَ الرَّأْيُ وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin ruḥi al-laylata ilā dhālika al-makāni wa-iḥdhar an tanāma fa-innaka tablughu al-marāma hādhā huwa al-raʾyu wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: But go tonight to that place, and beware that you sleep, for (then) you will reach the desire. This is the counsel, and peace!
sentences.i: But go to that place again tonight, and take care not to sleep, and you will have your wish. That is my advice, and there is no more to say.”
sentences.n: ruḥ, “go!”: the imperative of rāḥa, the everyday verb of going. marām / salām rhyme. wa-al-salām, “and peace”: that is all there is to it.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا أَنَامُ وَإِنَّمَا أَفْعَلُ مَا تَأْمُرِينِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā in shāʾa allāhu lā anāmu wa-innamā afʿalu mā taʾmurīnī bihi
sentences.l: And I said to her: If God wills, I will not sleep, and I will only do what you command me with.
sentences.i: I told her, “If God wills, I will not sleep; I will do just as you tell me.”
sentences.n: taʾmurīnī: Middle Arabic for Classical taʾmurīnanī, the indicative without its -na. amara bi-, “command (someone) to do”: bi- marks the thing commanded.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتِ ابْنَةُ عَمِّي وَأَتَتْ لِي بِالطَّعَامِ وَقَالَتْ لِي كُلِ الْآنَ مَا يَكْفِيكَ حَتَّى لَا يَبْقَى فِي خَاطِرِكَ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmati ibnatu ʿammī wa-atat lī bi-al-ṭaʿāmi wa-qālat lī kuli al-āna mā yakfīka ḥattā lā yabqā fī khāṭirika shayʾun
sentences.l: And the daughter of my uncle rose and brought to me the food, and said to me: Eat now what suffices you, so that there not remain in your mind a thing.
sentences.i: So my cousin got up and brought me food, and said to me, “Eat all you want now, so that you are left with no craving.”
sentences.n: atā bi-, “bring”: the verb takes bi- for the thing brought. khāṭir, “mind, inclination”: here, the appetite.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ كِفَايَتِي وَلَمَّا أَتَى اللَّيْلُ قَامَتْ بِنْتُ عَمِّي وَأَتَتْنِي بِبَدْلَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ وَأَلْبَسَتْنِي إِيَّاهَا وَحَلَّفَتْنِي أَنْ أَذْكُرَلَهَا الْبَيْتَ الْمَذْكُورَ وَحَذَّرَتْنِي مِنَ النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu kifāyatī wa-lammā atā al-laylu qāmat bintu ʿammī wa-atatnī bi-badlatin ʿaẓīmatin wa-albasatnī iyyāhā wa-ḥallafatnī an adhkura lahā al-bayta al-madhkūra wa-ḥadhdharatnī mina al-nawmi
sentences.l: And I ate my sufficiency; and when the night came, the daughter of my uncle rose and brought me a magnificent suit, and clothed me with it, and made-me-swear that I would mention to her the verse mentioned, and warned me of the sleep.
sentences.i: I ate my fill; and when night came my cousin got up and brought me a splendid suit of clothes and dressed me in it, and made me swear to recite that line of verse to the woman, and warned me against sleeping.
sentences.n: badla: a suit of clothes, a whole outfit. adhkura lahā, “that I mention to her”, is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِ بِنْتِ عَمِّي وَتَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَطَلَعْتُ ذَلِكَ الْمَقْعَدَ وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَجَعَلْتُ أَفْتَحُ عَيْنِي بِأَصَابِعِى وَأَهُزُّ رَأْسِي حِينَ جَنَّ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajtu min ʿindi binti ʿammī wa-tawajjahtu ilā al-bustāni wa-ṭalaʿtu dhālika al-maqʿada wa-naẓartu ilā al-bustāni wa-jaʿaltu aftaḥu ʿaynī bi-aṣābiʿī wa-ahuzzu raʾsī ḥīna janna al-laylu
sentences.l: Then I went out from the presence of the daughter of my uncle and turned-towards the garden, and went-up (into) that sitting-place, and looked at the garden; and I began opening my eye with my fingers and shaking my head, when the night grew-dark.
sentences.i: Then I left my cousin and made my way to the garden. I climbed up into the alcove and looked out over the garden, and as darkness fell I kept holding my eyes open with my fingers and shaking my head.
sentences.n: The print has جنّ المليل, a misprint for جنّ الليل, corrected here; the next night, which opens by repeating these lines, prints it correctly. janna al-laylu, “the night grew dark”, from the root of covering and hiding. jaʿaltu with an imperfect, “I began to …”; bi-aṣābiʿī, “with my fingers”: bi- of the instrument. min ʿindi, “from the presence of”, “from (being) with”.

sentences.t: فَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
